title: Freya and the Wreck
premise: Lena Dunmore has spent five years running salvage digs across three continents, outrunning the memory of the wreck that killed her father and broke her family apart. When her father's old rival, Marcus Vane, hires her crew to excavate that very wreck before the dry season ends, she takes the job for reasons she won't admit — the site log is missing, and only someone who dives it can prove what really happened down there. As the crew uncovers evidence that her father's death was no accident but a cover-up involving Vane himself, Lena must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the found family of misfits who depend on the payday. In the end, she gets the expedition home intact, burns Vane's contract, and hands the real findings to a coastal museum anonymously — justice delivered outside the law, loyalty kept, and the truth finally told to the one person who deserved it: herself.
about_author: Lior Eastwick is a former field technician turned novelist who writes adventure stories set in the liminal spaces between maps. They live near a working harbor and claim their best plot ideas arrive on the tide.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On a roadside dig in a drought-stricken province, Lena measures her life in distance traveled since her father's death. A wire arrives from Marcus Vane offering a contract too large to refuse — for a wreck she swore never to touch. Emotional beat: restless unease masked as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Crew That Chose Her
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She gathers her ragtag team: engineer Tomas, diver Priya, archivist Bo, and teenage runner Kit, each carrying their own reason to say yes to Vane's money. Over a shared meal they vote to take the job. Emotional beat: warmth of found family shadowed by what Lena isn't telling them.

chapters.title: Terms Written in Salt
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane meets Lena at a harbor office and lays out the contract: absolute secrecy, hard deadline at dry season's end, and a clause forbidding any publication of findings. He watches her sign, certain old guilt will keep her compliant. Emotional beat: predatory patience meeting quiet defiance.

chapters.title: The Road Back
chapters.summary: Kit's POV. The convoy travels toward the coast through country Kit has only heard about in Lena's nightmares. Kit maps the route, notices Lena go silent at every landmark, and begins piecing together that this coast means something. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into worry.

chapters.title: What the Tide Remembers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. First sight of the wreck site from the cliff road — the same black rocks, the same undertow. Lena walks the beach alone at night and finds the base camp already half-built by Vane's advance team. Emotional beat: grief ambushing her in a place she thought was only geography.

chapters.title: Dive One
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The first dive reveals the wreck remarkably preserved — and something wrong: hull damage inconsistent with any storm account Lena ever heard. Priya keeps it to herself, sensing the crew's fragile trust can't bear another secret yet. Emotional beat: professional thrill undercut by instinctive dread.

chapters.title: Bo's Ledger
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Cataloging recovered artifacts, Bo cross-references an old manifest and discovers cargo listed as lost was actually offloaded before the sinking — meaning someone profited from the disaster. Bo confronts Lena gently; Lena deflects. Emotional beat: the ache of loving someone who lies kindly.

chapters.title: Vane's Shadow
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas catches one of Vane's men photographing their equipment logs and quietly sabotages the camera. He warns Lena that Vane doesn't hire crews — he owns them. Emotional beat: protective anger, the crew closing ranks around its reluctant captain.

chapters.title: The Missing Logbook
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena admits to Priya why she came: her father's final dive log vanished after his death, and only the wreck itself can confirm or destroy what she suspects. Priya promises silence — and demands the whole truth next time. Emotional beat: confession as first act of trust.

chapters.title: Storm Out of Season
chapters.summary: Kit's POV. An unseasonal squall traps two divers below while Kit single-handedly runs the winch line under Tomas's shouted coaching. Everyone lives, but the deadline shrinks and tempers fray. Emotional beat: terror transformed into belonging — Kit stops being the kid.

chapters.title: Hull Breach
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Deep inside the wreck, Priya finds deliberate scuttling charges' residue and a sealed strongbox stamped with Vane's company mark. She photographs everything, then surfaces to find Vane's man watching the dive boat. Emotional beat: evidence in hand, safety gone.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane offers Lena a private deal: double pay, her father's logbook returned, in exchange for the strongbox and her signature burying the findings. He reveals he knows exactly what she's found. Emotional beat: temptation wearing the face of closure.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Weighs
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena weighs Vane's offer against the crew's livelihoods — the payday could set them all free, and the lie would be hers alone to carry. She tells the crew nothing yet, hating herself for it. Emotional beat: the loneliest hour of leadership.

chapters.title: Kit Runs
chapters.summary: Kit's POV. Kit overhears Vane's man threatening to report the crew's permits as fraudulent unless they comply. Kit rides overnight to the regional records office to verify the crew's paperwork is clean — and discovers Vane forged the complaint himself. Emotional beat: small courage with enormous stakes.

chapters.title: Fracture Line
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The crew learns Lena hid the strongbox discovery; trust cracks open into open argument on the beach. Tomas forces a vote: finish honest and broke, or take Vane's money and live with it. Emotional beat: found family tested not by enemies but by its own fault lines.

chapters.title: The Father's Log
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Reading her father's returned logbook, Lena deciphers his final entries: he had discovered Vane's cargo fraud and planned to report it. The 'accident' was arranged. Grief becomes purpose. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Dry Season Countdown
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. With days left before the dry season ends the dig legally, Bo devises a plan: document everything, duplicate the archive, and let Vane believe he's won until the last truck leaves. Emotional beat: cold clarity, the crew reunited around a shared deception aimed at the true liar.

chapters.title: The Last Dive
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya and Lena dive together to recover the final proof — her father's personal effects and the scuttling mechanism itself. Equipment fails; Lena nearly drowns reaching it. Emotional beat: descent as reckoning, surfacing as absolution.

chapters.title: Trucks at Dawn
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Loading out under Vane's surveillance, the crew executes Bo's shell game — decoy crates, hidden duplicates, Kit driving the real archive out in a produce truck. Vane inspects the site and finds exactly what he expects. Emotional beat: tension stretched to snapping, then sweet release.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane pays out, satisfied, and delivers a condescending toast to Lena's professionalism. Alone afterward, he opens the 'recovered' strongbox and finds it empty except for a copy of her father's logbook page and a note: 'The sea keeps accounts.' Emotional beat: victory inverted into exposure.

chapters.title: Justice Without Papers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Rather than go to authorities entangled with Vane's influence, Lena ships the full archive anonymously to a coastal maritime museum and a journalist, letting documented fact do what courts might not. The crew watches the news break from a diner booth, unpaid but unowned. Emotional beat: quiet triumph, truth told without permission asked.

chapters.title: Home Is a Heading
chapters.summary: Kit's POV. Weeks later, the crew votes on the next contract and, for the first time, Lena lets them choose the direction. Kit realizes Lena now measures life in people, not miles. On the horizon, the coast recedes — grieved, avenged, released. Emotional beat: arrival, at last, without arriving anywhere.
